glosses.notes: Refers to a period of unusually little rain that leaves fields, rivers, or reservoirs short of water.

examples.sentence: 去年春天一直不下雨，村里的人只好先把水送到田里，因为大家都怕这次旱灾再这样下去，到夏天连吃的东西都会少很多。
新闻说那边很久没有下大雨，不少地方已经开始少用水，连平时不太看天气的人也知道这次旱灾比往年更严重了。
去做调查的学生回来说，那边的地都干了，老人站着看了很久，只反复问一句，这次旱灾到底还要到哪一天才会完。

example_translations.translation: Last spring it simply did not rain, so the people in the village had to send water to the fields first, because everyone feared that if this drought kept going like this, even the amount of food by summer would be much smaller.

The news said that area had gone a long time without heavy rain, and many places had already started using less water, so even people who did not normally watch the weather closely knew this drought was more serious than in past years.

The students who went to investigate came back saying the land there had all dried up. The old man stood there looking for a long time and only kept asking one thing: on what day would this drought finally end?

glosses.notes: Usually refers to aviation, airlines, or the air-transport industry rather than one single flight.

examples.sentence: 这场大雾刚到城外，机场的大屏幕就改了好几次时间，航空公司的工作人员一直在前面解释情况，怕后面排队的人越等越急。
孩子从小喜欢看天上的飞机，所以一听说航空公司周末让大家进去看，他就拉着爸爸很早出门，想先看看那些平时只在电视里见过的大飞机。
这几年不少年轻人想学航空管理，不只是因为工资看起来高一点，也是因为他们觉得以后城市和城市之间的来往会越来越离不开它。

example_translations.translation: As soon as the heavy fog reached the edge of the city, the airport screen changed the times again and again, and the airline staff kept explaining the situation at the front because they feared the people waiting in line would grow more anxious the longer they waited.

The child had loved watching airplanes in the sky since he was small, so as soon as he heard that the airline would let people go in and look around on the weekend, he pulled his dad out early because he wanted to see those big planes he had only seen on television before.

In recent years many young people have wanted to study aviation management, not only because the pay seems a little higher, but also because they feel cities will rely on aviation more and more in the future.

glosses.notes: An adverb used before verbs or adjectives to stress a complete lack of hesitation, regret, fear, or some other attitude.

examples.sentence: 听完对方的解释以后，她的脸色还是一点没变，回答的时候也毫不犹豫，好像来之前就已经把每个问题都想清楚了。
那位老医生说起最难的几年时，语气一直很平，但是大家都知道，他当年留下照顾那些病人，毫不后悔，因为那时他要是也走了，很多人就没人管了。
记者刚问到那个最敏感的问题，他就毫不客气地指出报告里的漏洞，还说如果连这个都看不见，后面的讨论根本没有意义。

example_translations.translation: After hearing the other side’s explanation, her expression did not change at all, and she answered without the slightest hesitation, as if she had already thought through every question before coming.

When the old doctor spoke about the hardest years, his tone stayed calm, but everyone knew that he did not regret at all staying behind to care for those patients, because if he too had left at that time, many people would have had no one to look after them.

The moment the reporter asked the most sensitive question, he bluntly pointed out the holes in the report and said that if people could not even see that, the rest of the discussion had no meaning at all.

glosses.notes: Usually appears before nouns such as 办法, 准备, or 兴趣 to show that something is completely absent.

examples.sentence: 第一次上台的人要是毫无准备，站到灯光下面以后往往连最熟的开头也会一下子忘掉，只能边想边看台下老师的表情。
大家开了两个小时的会，对最重要的问题还是毫无办法，所以负责人只好把计划分成几部分，让每个小组先回去算一算。
他表面上说得很轻松，其实心里并不是毫无压力，只是不想让刚来的同事一开始就觉得这里什么都很难。

example_translations.translation: If someone goes on stage for the first time completely unprepared, once they stand under the lights they often forget even the opening they know best and can only think while watching the teacher’s expression below the stage.

Everyone held a two-hour meeting, but they still had no solution at all for the most important problem, so the person in charge had to divide the plan into several parts and let each group go back and work through it once.
He spoke lightly on the surface, but in truth he was not without pressure at all; he just did not want the new coworkers to feel from the very beginning that everything here was difficult.

glosses.notes: A unit for measuring very small lengths or thicknesses, often used when even a tiny difference matters.

examples.sentence: 师傅把那块玻璃放到灯下又看了一遍，说边上只差一毫米，装进旧窗以后就可能一直关不严，最好现在就重新改一改。
医生给家里人解释的时候，用笔在屏幕上比着说，这个地方虽然只多出几毫米，但是现在要不要动它，还得看他今天晚上还会不会疼。
设计图上那条线看着没什么分别，但是真做的时候，只要多两毫米，后面的门就会一直碰到那一边，声音也很明显。

example_translations.translation: The worker put the piece of glass under the light and checked it again, saying the edge was off by only one millimeter, but once it was fitted into the old window it might never close tightly, so it would be best to adjust it again now.

When the doctor explained things to the family, he gestured at the screen with his pen and said that although this spot was only a few millimeters larger, whether it should be touched right now still depended on whether the patient would keep hurting tonight.

The line on the design drawing did not look very different, but once the real work was done, even two extra millimeters would make the door behind it keep hitting the side, and the sound would be obvious too.

glosses.notes: A unit for measuring small amounts of liquid, especially in medicine, experiments, and product sizes.

examples.sentence: 护士换完药以后，又拿起杯子看了一眼，提醒家属先别让他一下子喝太多，先慢慢喝几十毫升，看胃里会不会不舒服。
做实验的学生把两种液体倒进量杯时，只多了五毫升，颜色就和老师给的结果完全不一样，所以大家只好从头再来一次。
卖东西的人介绍这瓶香水的时候，没有先说牌子多有名，而是先提醒客人看清有多少毫升，因为三十毫升和五十毫升的价格差得并不小。

example_translations.translation: After changing the medicine, the nurse glanced at the cup again and reminded the family not to let him drink too much at once. He should slowly drink a few dozen milliliters first and see whether his stomach felt uncomfortable.

When the students doing the experiment poured the two liquids into the measuring cup, they added only five milliliters too much, and the color turned out completely different from the teacher’s result, so everyone had to start over.

When the salesperson introduced this bottle of perfume, they did not begin by talking about how famous the brand was. Instead, they first reminded the customer to look carefully at how many milliliters it held, because the price difference between thirty milliliters and fifty milliliters was not small.

glosses.notes: A literary or emotional intensifier used before adjectives or verbs to mean very or really, often in exclamatory scenes.

examples.sentence: 广场上一放音乐，卖吃的和看戏的人就都围了过来，四周一下子好不热闹，连站在远处的人都忍不住往前走。
她原来只是想把旧照片整理一下，没想到一边看一边讲，从小学说到工作，坐在旁边的母女俩笑得好不开心，连晚饭都差点忘了做。
过了很多年，在车站又见面的同学，先是谁也不敢认，等名字一对上，两个人就在路边说得好不痛快，后来把车都错过了。

example_translations.translation: As soon as the music started in the square, the people selling food and the people watching the show all gathered around, and the whole area suddenly became so lively that even those standing far away could not help moving forward.

She had only meant to sort through some old photos, but as she looked and talked, moving from primary school all the way to work, the mother and daughter sitting beside her laughed so happily that they almost forgot to make dinner.

After many years had passed, the classmates who met again at the station did not dare recognize each other at first. Once they matched the names, they talked so freely by the roadside that they later missed their rides.

glosses.notes: Refers to the positive feeling or liking someone gradually develops toward a person, place, or thing.

examples.sentence: 她第一次和新同事一起出门办事，本来还有点紧张，但是对方一直都照顾她，等车到站的时候，她心里已经有了不少好感。
这家店看上去并不特别，但是里面的人记得老客人爱吃什么，所以很多人第一次来只是看一看，后来慢慢对它有了好感。
他在台上回答问题的时候没有故意表现自己，反而因为那份自然和认真，让台下原来很怀疑的人也多了几分好感。

example_translations.translation: It was her first time going out to handle work with a new coworker, and she had been a little nervous, but the other person looked after her the whole way, so by the time the train arrived she already had a very favorable impression.

This shop did not look especially special, but the people inside remembered what the regular customers liked to eat, so many people only looked around the first time they came and later gradually developed a good feeling toward it.

When he answered questions on stage, he did not try to show off. Instead, that natural and serious manner made even the people who had been doubtful below the stage feel a little more favorably toward him.

glosses.notes: Means only after a lot of effort, waiting, or delay; it often appears with 才 to stress how hard it was.

examples.sentence: 大家在雨里等了快一个小时，好容易才把设备全搬进大厅，结果刚接上电，负责人又说顺序还得重新排。
她陪老人跑了好几家医院，好容易约到那位专家，本来以为终于能安心一点，没想到检查前还得再补一份材料。
这条山路以前一下雨就封，村里的人等了很多年，好容易等到桥修好，孩子们去镇里上学才不用天不亮就出门。

example_translations.translation: Everyone waited in the rain for nearly an hour and only with great difficulty managed to carry all the equipment into the hall, but as soon as it was plugged in, the person in charge said the order still had to be rearranged.

She accompanied the old man to several hospitals and only with a lot of effort got an appointment with that specialist. She thought they could finally relax a little, but before the examination they still had to submit another document.

In the past this mountain road would close whenever it rained. The people in the village waited for many years and only with great difficulty lived to see the bridge repaired, and only then did the children no longer have to leave before dawn to study in town.

glosses.notes: Describes people who warmly receive guests and naturally make visitors feel welcome and cared for.

examples.sentence: 那家旅馆不大，但是老板好客，客人进门以后，他就先给水，还把晚上可以去的地方慢慢讲清楚。
他第一次去朋友老家，本来还怕自己话不多，没想到对方一家人太好客，饭还没有上完，就已经把第二天的安排都替他想好了。
导游说这个地方出名不只是风景好，也是因为这里的人向来好客，外地人问路时，常常还没开口，对方就先把方向说得很清楚。

example_translations.translation: That inn was not big, but the owner was hospitable. After guests came in, he first gave them water and then slowly explained clearly where they could go in the evening.

It was his first time visiting his friend’s hometown, and he had worried that he was not very talkative, but the other family turned out to be so hospitable that before all the dishes were even served, they had already planned the next day for him.

The guide said this place was famous not only for its scenery but also because the people here had always been hospitable. When outsiders ask for directions, often before they can even begin speaking, the other person has already explained the direction clearly.

glosses.notes: Describes someone who truly likes learning and keeps asking, reading, or practicing beyond what is required.

examples.sentence: 老师提起那个最安静的学生时，总说他不只是学习认真，更难得的是人很好学，连下课以后别人急着走的时候，他还会把没懂的地方写下来再问。
刚进公司的人里，他未必经验最多，但是大家都愿意带他，因为他确实好学，别人提醒过的事，他很少再错。
山里有个人没上过多少学，但是一到新机器出来的时候，还是和年轻人一样好学，晚上以后也要把书慢慢看完。

example_translations.translation: Whenever the teacher mentioned that quiet student, she would say that what was special was not only that he studied seriously, but also that he was eager to learn. Even after class, when others were hurrying to leave, he would still write down what he had not understood and ask again.

Among the people who had just joined the company, he might not have had the most experience, but everyone was willing to guide him because he really was eager to learn. Once others reminded him of something, he rarely got it wrong again.

There was a person in the mountains who had not gone to school much, but whenever a new machine appeared, he was still as eager to learn as a young person and would keep reading the book slowly after evening came.

glosses.notes: Can mean to call on people to act or, as a noun, a public appeal that tries to gather support.

examples.sentence: 市里发出号召以后，不少大学生周末都去河边捡垃圾，不是因为有人天天检查，而是大家真觉得这条河不能再这样脏下去了。
校长在会上号召老师把旧电脑整理出来给乡下学校时，原来最犹豫的几个人后来反而最先把名单交了上来。
医生在节目里号召大家按时体检，不是想吓人，而是怕很多病等到身体明显不舒服的时候，已经错过最好处理的时间。

example_translations.translation: After the city issued a public call, many university students went to pick up trash by the river on weekends, not because someone was checking every day, but because people truly felt the river could not stay this dirty any longer.

When the principal called on the teachers at the meeting to sort out old computers for rural schools, the few people who had hesitated the most at first later turned out to be the first to hand in their lists.

The doctor appealed to everyone on the program to get checkups on time, not to scare people, but because many illnesses have already missed the best time for treatment by the moment the body feels obviously unwell.

glosses.notes: Used when departments, schools, records, or other separate things are brought together and handled as one.

examples.sentence: 两个办公室原来各做各的表，月底总要反复检查，后来领导决定把流程合并以后，少了很多重复的电话，也没人再说同一件事要写两次。
医院把挂号和付钱的地方合并以后，前面排队的人看起来更多了，但是人来回走的次数少了，所以最后还是快了不少。
这两所小学校学生越来越少，家长一开始都不愿意合并，后来老师把上课和接孩子说清楚以后，大家才慢慢接受。

example_translations.translation: The two offices used to make separate forms and had to check them again and again at the end of every month. After the leaders decided to merge the process, there were far fewer repeated phone calls and no one said the same matter had to be written down twice anymore.
After the hospital merged the registration and payment areas, the line in front looked longer, but people had to walk back and forth fewer times, so in the end it still became much faster.

The student numbers at these two small schools kept dropping, and the parents were unwilling to merge them at first. Only after the teachers clearly explained the classes and how the children would be picked up did everyone gradually accept it.

glosses.notes: Can mean to synthesize materials or to combine separate sounds, images, or parts into one finished result.

examples.sentence: 这种材料不是从地里直接挖出来的，而是研究人员在实验室里一步一步合成的，所以成本高的时候，工厂也不敢一下子做太多。
老师给学生放那段影片的时候，特意停下来说明，说里面海边的声音不是现场录的，而是后来拿几种声音合成出来的。
医生解释报告时说，这种药的主要成分虽然可以人工合成，但是真正难的是让它放了很久以后还能一直稳定。

example_translations.translation: This material is not dug directly out of the ground. It is synthesized step by step by researchers in the laboratory, so when costs are high, the factory does not dare produce too much at once.

When the teacher played that film clip for the students, he deliberately paused to explain that the sounds of the seaside in it had not been recorded on site, but had later been created by combining several different sounds.

When the doctor explained the report, he said that although the main ingredient of this medicine can be synthesized artificially, the real difficulty is keeping it stable even after it has been stored for a long time.

glosses.notes: Refers to peace as the opposite of war or violent conflict, and also to a calm way of settling disputes.

examples.sentence: 老人年轻时真正见过战争，所以每次看见孩子在门口跑来跑去，他都会说，能让下一代把这种日子当平常，才说明和平真的很不容易。
记者去采访那场纪念活动时，现场没有太多口号，大家只是安静地放下白花，因为不少人觉得说再多，也不如提醒后人好好守住和平。
两国学生在线上说话的时候，原来只想练一练，后来谈到各自家里的故事，大家才更明白为什么老师总把和平放在课上最前面。

example_translations.translation: The old man had truly seen war when he was young, so every time he saw children running back and forth by the doorway, he would say that only when the next generation can treat such days as ordinary does it show how hard peace really is to keep.

When the reporter went to cover that memorial event, there were not many slogans on site. People simply laid down white flowers quietly, because many felt that saying more was less important than reminding later generations to guard peace well.

When students from the two countries spoke online, they had only wanted to practice a little at first. Later, when they talked about stories from their families, everyone understood more clearly why the teacher always puts peace at the very front of the lesson.

glosses.notes: Describes sounds, colors, relationships, or arrangements that fit together smoothly and pleasantly.

examples.sentence: 新来的指挥没有急着改每个人的习惯，而是先让大家多听彼此的声音，所以乐队排了几次以后，整体就比以前和谐多了。
这个小区楼不高，人也杂，但是负责的人一直把地方收拾得很干净，谁家有事也愿意先商量，所以住久了反而显得很和谐。
这幅画最吸引人的不是颜色有多亮，而是深浅放在一起特别和谐，就连原来觉得自己不懂画的人，也能一下子看出那种安静的力量。

example_translations.translation: The new conductor did not rush to change each person’s habits. Instead, he first let everyone listen more to one another’s sound, so after a few rehearsals the orchestra became much more harmonious than before.

The buildings in this neighborhood are not tall and the residents are mixed, but the people in charge keep the place very clean, and families are willing to discuss things first when something comes up, so after living there a long time it actually feels harmonious.

What draws people most in this painting is not how bright the colors are, but how harmoniously the light and dark shades are placed together. Even people who thought they did not understand painting can immediately sense that quiet strength.

glosses.notes: Refers to the most central part, idea, or force that determines how the whole thing works.

examples.sentence: 讨论了半天以后，主持人忽然把纸一合，说大家先别急着补细节，真正的核心问题只有一个，就是这笔钱到底准备替谁解决什么困难。
这座老城这几年变化很快，但是做计划的人一直坚持不要动最核心的地方，因为一旦把那些老店和老路都拆了，再新的楼也留不住这里原来的样子。
他以为自己已经把报告写得很完整了，结果老师只看了第一页就说，材料虽然多，但是核心意思一直没有讲清楚，所以别人很难知道你到底想证明什么。

example_translations.translation: After everyone had discussed it for a long time, the host suddenly closed his papers and said that before filling in details, they should remember there was only one real core problem: exactly whose difficulty this money was meant to solve.

This old city has changed quickly in recent years, but the people making the plan have always insisted that the most central area should not be touched, because once those old shops and roads are torn down, no matter how new the buildings are, they will not preserve the city’s original look.

He thought he had already written a very complete report, but after looking only at the first page, the teacher said that although there was a lot of material, the core meaning had never been explained clearly, so others would have a hard time knowing what he was actually trying to prove.

glosses.notes: An interjection used to call out to someone, get attention, or suddenly break an awkward silence in speech.

examples.sentence: 他刚走到门口，就听见后面有人大声说嘿，回头看，原来是以前的同学，手里还拿着他最爱吃的东西，两个人都笑了。
司机正要关门的时候，一个孩子在雨里边跑边喊“嘿，等一下”，车里原本都低头看手机的人一下子全把目光抬了起来。
录节目那天现场有点冷，主持人上台先笑着说了一句“嘿，大家别这么安静”，台下的人这才慢慢放松下来。

example_translations.translation: He had just reached the doorway when he heard someone behind him loudly say “hey.” When he turned back to look, it was a classmate from earlier years, still holding the food he loved most, and the two of them both laughed.

Just as the driver was about to close the doors, a child came running in the rain and shouted, “Hey, wait a second!” and all the people on the bus who had been looking down at their phones suddenly lifted their eyes.
The atmosphere on the day of recording was a little stiff, so when the host walked on stage he smiled and said, “Hey, don’t be so quiet,” and only then did the people below the stage slowly relax.

glosses.notes: Can describe physical darkness and also difficult periods where people feel lost, trapped, or unable to see a way out.

examples.sentence: 山里的电突然断掉以后，整条路一下子变得很黑暗，走在前面的人只好先停下来，等后面的人把灯一个一个地打开。
电影并没有一直拍得很黑，真正让人难受的是那种明明快看见出口，却又被黑暗重新包住的感觉。
他谈起那段最黑暗的日子时，没有把自己说得多可怜，只是反复提到，要不是身边一直有人拉着他，他可能早就撑不下去了。

example_translations.translation: After the electricity suddenly went out in the mountains, the whole road suddenly became very dark. The people walking in front had to stop first and wait for those behind to turn on the lights one by one.
The film was not shot dark all the way through. What really made people uneasy was the feeling of almost seeing the exit, only to be wrapped by darkness again.

When he talked about that darkest period, he did not describe himself as especially pitiful. He only kept saying that if people around him had not kept pulling him along, he might have collapsed long ago.

glosses.notes: Refers to a visible or discoverable trace left behind by use, movement, damage, or some earlier event.

examples.sentence: 昨天晚上下过一场大雨，早上去看的时候，台阶上还留着很清楚的水和泥的痕迹，所以管事的人一眼就知道半夜确实有人从后门进来过。
这张旧桌子表面有不少使用痕迹，但是他不肯全改，因为他觉得正是这些小地方，才让人看得出它有多少年了。
大家把那个地方围住以后，没有先让人随便进出，而是先去看窗那边的几处痕迹，因为真正有用的线索常常就在这些地方。

example_translations.translation: A heavy rain fell last night, and when people went to look in the morning, clear traces of water and mud still remained on the steps, so the person in charge immediately knew someone really had come in from the back gate during the night.

There are many marks of use on the surface of this old table, but he refuses to change them all, because he feels it is exactly these small details that let people see how many years it has been around.

After everyone surrounded that place, they did not first let people move in and out casually. Instead, they first went to look at the few traces near the window, because truly useful clues are often right in places like that.

glosses.notes: Can describe someone as harsh or ruthless, and it also appears in expressions like 狠心 when someone forces themselves to act firmly.

examples.sentence: 教练平时说话不重，但是比赛前忽然特别狠，谁动作慢一点都要重来，因为他知道大家离上场还差最后一点力。
母亲嘴上说得再狠，真看到孩子半夜发烧，还是第一时间穿上衣服抱着人往医院跑，一路上连鞋带开了都顾不上系。
他本来舍不得关那家小店，但是一看就知道再拖下去只会欠得更多，只好狠心把最后几件东西都低价卖了。

example_translations.translation: The coach was not usually heavy in his words, but before the match he suddenly became especially harsh, making anyone whose movements were a little slow start again, because he knew everyone was still missing that final bit of strength before going on.

No matter how harsh the mother sounded, once she really saw her child burning with fever in the middle of the night, she still threw on clothes at once and carried the child toward the hospital, not even stopping to tie her shoelaces when they came loose on the way.
He had not wanted to close that little shop, but one look was enough to see that delaying further would only create more debt, so he had to harden his heart and sell the last few things off cheaply.

glosses.notes: Can express strong hatred, but it is also often used for deep regret directed at oneself or a painful past event.

examples.sentence: 年轻的时候他只顾着往外跑，等父亲真的老了，才发现自己会的道理很多，能陪在身边的时间却太少，所以每次想起这件事都很恨自己。
她并不恨那个抢走机会的人，真正让她难受的是，自己当时明明还有话能说清楚，却因为害怕当场什么也没讲。
电影里那个人一直说自己最恨别人骗他，但是最后大家才明白，他其实更恨当年那个没有勇气出来的自己。

example_translations.translation: When he was young he only cared about going out into the world. Only after his father truly grew old did he realize that although he knew many principles, he had spent far too little time by his father’s side, so every time he thought of it he bitterly hated himself.

She did not actually hate the person who took the opportunity away. What truly hurt her was that at the time she clearly still had things she could have explained, yet because of fear she said nothing on the spot.
In the film, that person kept saying he hated being lied to most, but in the end everyone understood that what he hated even more was his former self, the self who lacked the courage to come forward.

glosses.notes: Often refers to something lying across or sideways, and it appears in forms like 横着, 横穿, and 横线.

examples.sentence: 这块牌子原来是竖着挂的，风一大就老撞墙，师傅来了一次以后把它改成横着装，门口的人进出才不总被声音吓一跳。
孩子们放学以后总爱从草地中间横穿过去，管事的人起初只是在旁边提醒，后来怕雨后路滑，才慢慢把那条小路重新铺平。
老师把地图展开以后，先画了一条横线，让大家别急着背城市名字，而是先看山和河大概把这个地方分成了几部分。

example_translations.translation: This sign had originally been hung vertically, and whenever the wind picked up it kept hitting the wall. After the worker came once and changed it to a horizontal position, people entering and leaving the doorway stopped getting startled by the noise all the time.

After school the children always liked to cut across the middle of the grass. At first the person in charge only reminded them from the side, but later, worried the path would be slippery after rain, gradually had that small path paved flat again.

After the teacher opened the map, she first drew a horizontal line and told everyone not to rush into memorizing city names, but to look first at how the mountains and rivers roughly divided the place into several parts.

glosses.notes: Used when judging value, ability, or results by weighing different factors rather than looking at only one sign.

examples.sentence: 招人不能只看一张简历写得多漂亮，真正负责的人还得看他有压力的时候怎么说话做事，这样才比较能衡量以后能不能放心把事交给他。
这家店值不值得长期合作，不是用一次活动的销量就能衡量的，老板更在意对方出问题的时候愿不愿意马上出来处理。
医生提醒家属，老人恢复得快不快，不能只拿今天和昨天来衡量，还要看他一周以后能不能自己下床、吃饭、说清楚话。

example_translations.translation: Hiring someone cannot depend only on how polished a resume looks. A truly responsible person also has to see how the candidate speaks and acts when under pressure, because that is a better way to judge whether important work can be entrusted to them later.

Whether this shop is worth working with over the long term cannot be measured by the sales from a single event. The owner cares more about whether the other side is willing to step forward and deal with problems right away when something goes wrong.

The doctor reminded the family that how quickly the old man was recovering could not be measured only by comparing today with yesterday. They also needed to see whether after a week he could get out of bed, eat, and speak clearly by himself.

glosses.notes: Describes something large in scale or ambition, such as a scene, plan, theme, or vision.

examples.sentence: 导演说这部片子最难的不是场面不够宏大，而是人物要真实，因为如果观众只记住灯光和音乐，回家以后很快就会把故事忘掉。
晚上站在桥上看城市的时候，很多人都会先觉得眼前的工程十分宏大，但是真正让本地人安心的，还是那些医院学校和地铁是不是都有了。
这本书开头写得很宏大，从天到地都像要说一说，但是老师读了一半就提醒作者，越是想谈大问题，越要先把一个人的经历写清楚。

example_translations.translation: The director said the hardest part of this film was not making the scenes grand enough, but making the characters feel real, because if viewers remember only the lights and music, they will forget the story soon after going home.

When people stand on the bridge at night and look at the city, many first feel that the project before their eyes is extremely grand. But what truly reassures local people is whether the hospitals, schools, and subway are all there as well.

The opening of this book is written on a very grand scale, as if it wants to talk about everything from sky to earth. But halfway through, the teacher reminded the author that the more you want to discuss big issues, the more you need to write one person’s experience clearly first.
